baseline_best_term.rule: per clause type, the one word or word pair whose presence best predicts the type at contract level (F1) on the training contracts of each fold; a sentence is flagged when it contains it

diagnostic.fit_rule: document-level micro F1 over all 36 types, training contracts vs held-out contracts (each fold's model scored on its own training contracts with its own thresholds): overfits when training minus held-out is 0.10 or more; underfits when the gap is under 0.10 and training F1 is under 0.90; otherwise neither

match_rules.document: a contract contains a clause type when the lawyers marked at least one span of it; the model finds it when at least one sentence is flagged
match_rules.flagged: a sentence is flagged when its probability is at or above the clause type's threshold
match_rules.positive: a sentence is positive for a clause type when it overlaps a lawyer-marked span of that type by at least one non-space character
match_rules.sentence: the server's own sentence splitter; heading-only lines are dropped, as the server does
match_rules.span_recall: share of lawyer-marked spans that overlap at least one flagged sentence
match_rules.strict: a sentence is positive only when at least half of its non-space characters lie inside lawyer-marked spans of that type (reported beside the main rule)

classifier.model: logistic regression, one per clause type

recipe.near_duplicates: contracts with Jaccard similarity >= 0.8 on word 5-grams are kept in one fold
recipe.threshold: best document-level F1 on a 0.01 grid (0.01 to 0.99), ties to the higher threshold, from out-of-fold probabilities on training contracts only

switch_off_rule: A clause type is switched off (the model is not used for it, and extract_key_terms does not report it) when its cross-validated document-level F1, pooled over the five held-out folds, is below 0.50. Switched-off types are still scored and listed separately in the results, outside the averages.
